summary.headline: VA Tech Wabag H1 FY27 order book hit record Rs 20,207 crore and net cash crossed Rs 1,000 crore; H1 PAT up ~30% to Rs 195 crore.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue crossed Rs 1,000 crore with PAT above Rs 100 crore, described as the highest-ever Q2. Consolidated H1 revenue rose 20.3% YoY to Rs 1,887 crore, EBITDA rose about 21% to Rs 261 crore (margin ~14%), and PAT rose about 30% to Rs 195 crore (margin 10.3% vs 9.6%). Order book closed H1 at a record Rs 20,207 crore on H1 order intake of over Rs 5,200 crore, and net cash (incl. HAM) reached Rs 1,036 crore. Management says profit growth continues to outpace revenue growth, with the Kuwait and Reliance wins anchoring the intake.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 1,587 crore / Rs 227 crore / Rs 169 crore

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 950 crore at FY26 end
15th consecutive quarter of positive net cash

segments.name: Geography (H1 revenue)
segments.commentary: International markets contributed 54% of H1 revenue and India 46%. Order book is roughly 55:45 India:international per management, with Middle East about 60-70% of the international book.

segments.name: Business mix (H1 revenue)
segments.commentary: EPC was 82% and O&M 18% of H1 revenue. Management is building O&M toward a 20% share of revenue.

segments.name: Order wins
segments.commentary: Kuwait MEW desalination (60 MIGD, with Highscope, plus 5-year O&M post EPC, about USD 400 mn per Q&A); Reliance Jamnagar desalination 201 MLD expandable to 302 MLD plus 72 MLD remineralisation; Reliance repeat ETP order; Ajman (UAE) wastewater; Adani ZLD; Bengaluru and Surat water projects; Delhi Jal Board medium order; Vienna waterworks (Austria).

guidance_outlook: Medium-term targets reiterated: revenue growth 15-20%, EBITDA margin 13-15%, ROCE about 20%, ROE about 15%, O&M at 20% of revenue, and sustained positive net cash.
Management expects a bumper order-intake period over the next 12-18 months, with the aim of becoming preferred bidder on several large Middle East bids within one or two quarters.
Bangladesh World Bank-funded project may see about six months of delay, which management says it will absorb without margin impact.
Management targets at least Rs 500-600 crore operating cash flow for FY27 on a consolidated basis, described as an endeavour (raised by an analyst, not formally guided).
RIPB20 five-year strategy to be unveiled at the annual investor meet in May 2027.
Alhaya (Saudi) commissioning targeted in Q4 FY27; Kuwait, Ajman and other new projects are early-stage.
capex_capacity: Alhaya (Saudi) project: mechanical completion in final stage; civil works 80-85% complete; commissioning targeted in Q4 FY27.
Rastalura (Saudi) project: mechanical construction complete, pre-commissioning underway, hydro-test targeted shortly.
Chennai Metro 400 MLD desalination plant (Peru) in India: about 90% concreting done (about 1 million cubic metres), 7 million safe man-hours, schedule on track for completion in the coming year.
Multilateral-funded projects in Nepal/South East Asia: procurement about 100% complete, civil about 70%; liquid-stream commissioning targeted by end FY27.
Bangladesh project: engineering nearly complete, ordering about 90% done, 30-40% material dispatched, civil works 30-40%.
Bengaluru Manohali and Delhi Jal Board Mitron projects progressing; Delhi outfall pipeline supplies to start this month.
demand_pricing: Management described bidding activity as at a peak, with a large enquiry pipeline across Middle East, Europe, India municipal and industrial segments.
Middle East: Saudi Arabia new-project awards described as slower and more cautious; Kuwait, UAE and some preferred-bidder projects are moving.
India: enquiries from Tamil Nadu (a 400 MLD North Chennai desalination plant announced), Bengaluru, Delhi, MP, Rajasthan, and industrial clients including Reliance and DPCL.
Europe: activity picked up after subdued quarters, with two contracts won in the cluster.
Sunrise sectors (semiconductor, data centres, PV solar, hydrogen): small modular orders, 12-15 month execution cycles, separate vertical formed; no order-intake quantum guidance given.
Commodity price inflation: Indian contracts have escalation formulas; international contracts are hedged/locked by placing major orders early. Margin guidance of 13-15% accounts for this.

qa_highlights.question: How are Middle East supply-chain disruptions and commodity pricing affecting execution and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no major dent to timelines or margins so far, as most work has moved to site. The main issue is shipment delays; the client has agreed to longer sea routes, with air freight for critical items. A strategy will be needed if the situation does not improve in 6 months.

qa_highlights.question: Will Middle East pipeline conversion be slower given the geopolitical situation?
qa_highlights.answer: Some delay is expected as governments reassess investment baskets. Kuwait (about USD 400 mn with JV partner) and UAE Ajman have moved to execution; Saudi is slower and cautious, though some preferred-bidder projects are starting.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the domestic and international bid pipeline over 12-18 months?
qa_highlights.answer: No quantified pipeline was given. Management is bullish, with large enquiries in Middle East and India, and expects a bumper ordering period over 12-18 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EPC/O&M mix in order intake, and what is the Alhaya civil status?
qa_highlights.answer: Kuwait and Reliance, which together are about 80% of H1 intake, are EPC-focused with the customer or partner doing civil. Alhaya civil works are over 80-85% complete.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin improvement structural, and how are execution and payment risks managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin has stayed within 13-15% for five to six years, driven by project mix and execution. Management prefers sovereign, multilateral or LC-backed contracts and spreads risk across geographies and currencies.

qa_highlights.question: Why was employee expense high in Q2, and does it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to annual increments, performance pay and wage code impact, with no one-offs; it expects normalisation over the year.

risks_watch: Shipping and logistics delays to Middle East sites; if unresolved in 6 months, a new delivery strategy will be needed.
Slower Saudi Arabia new-award pipeline and PPP-model shift in Middle East water.
Bangladesh project delay of about six months (absorbed, not expected to affect margin).
Commodity inflation, passed through on Indian escalation contracts and hedged internationally.
Indosol solar project still needs about 100 acres of balance land; sunrise-segment orders are small and modular.
Management succession planning (son Rohan Mithil handles Middle East, GCC and Africa) and reliance on knowledge repositories.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on order momentum, cash and margins, citing record levels. Cautious on Middle East shipping and Saudi award timing, with management saying the disruption has not yet affected execution.

adds.what: Chennai Metro 400 MLD desalination plant (India), ~90% concreting done, completion in coming year
Multilateral-funded projects in Nepal/South East Asia, liquid-stream commissioning targeted by end FY27

growth.why: Management reiterated 15-20% medium-term revenue growth, backed by a record Rs 20,207 crore order book (about 10x FY26 revenue run-rate would be overstated; order book covers multiple years), H1 order intake over Rs 5,200 crore, and Saudi/India/Nepal projects commissioning over the next 1-3 quarters.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: H1 PAT margin rose to 10.3% from 9.6% and standalone PAT grew 29% vs revenue 19%, with gross margin held in the 13-15% band for five to six years and EBITDA margin guided at 13-15%; management says profit growth continues to outpace revenue, though Q2 employee cost rose on increments and wage code.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Alhaya (Saudi) commissioning targeted Q4 FY27, Rastalura pre-commissioning underway, Chennai Metro 400 MLD about 90% concreted with completion in coming year, and Nepal/SE Asia liquid-stream commissioning by end FY27, so new capacity comes live in the window though these are existing-project completions rather than new plants.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 revenue grew 20.3% YoY to Rs 1,887 crore against a record Rs 20,207 crore order book and over Rs 5,200 crore H1 intake; management reiterated 15-20% revenue growth, though Saudi awards are slower and Bangladesh slips about six months.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex plan or utilisation figure was given; the business is EPC/O&M and asset-light, with HAM and project capex already committed rather than a new capex announcement signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is bullish on a bumper 12-18 month ordering period and aims to become preferred bidder on several large Middle East bids within one or two quarters, but it only reiterated (did not raise) the 15-20% growth and 13-15% margin targets.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Middle East shipping delays could force a new delivery strategy if unresolved in 6 months, Saudi awards are slower, and Bangladesh is about six months late, though management says margins are unaffected so far.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Sunrise-sector vertical (semiconductor, data centres, PV, hydrogen) has small modular orders with 12-15 month cycles, but no quantum or launch timing was given; RIPB20 strategy is only due May 2027.

rows.label: Record Rs 20,207 crore order book, bumper ordering period
rows.why: Order book hit a lifetime high of Rs 20,207 crore with H1 intake over Rs 5,200 crore, Kuwait (about USD 400 mn) and Reliance together about 80% of intake, and management expects a bumper ordering period with large Middle East and India enquiries.

rows.label: Net working capital days falling
rows.why: NWC days fell to 101 from 104 at March 2026 and H1 operating cash flow was Rs 225 crore (about 1.1x PAT), with management targeting at least Rs 500-600 crore operating cash flow for FY27, described as an endeavour rather than formal guidance.

rows.label: Middle East preferred-bidder wins (Saudi, Kuwait, UAE)
rows.why: Management aims to become preferred bidder on several large Middle East bids within one or two quarters, but says Saudi awards are slower and cautious while Kuwait and Ajman have moved to execution.

tone.note: Management was confident on record order book, net cash of Rs 1,036 crore and margins held at 13-15%, while cautious on Middle East shipping delays and slower Saudi award timing; analysts pushed on the Middle East pipeline conversion, commodity pricing and the employee cost jump.
